# Phase 2: OPDS Per-User Authentication - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-05-31
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Mode:** Auto-generated (autonomous — decisions pinned by the cross-repo contract)

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

OPDS clients (android-reader and standard OPDS readers) authenticate per user
against the documented wire contract, and reading progress reported over the
OPDS-authenticated path is attributed to the right account. In scope: a Prisma
token model (hashed at rest), an in-route auth guard on all OPDS endpoints
(they are deliberately middleware-exempt), per-user progress attribution for
the OPDS path, and a web UI for users to mint/label/list/revoke their tokens.
Out of scope: per-library token scoping (later milestone), OPDS feed
pagination (Phase 3 / later), and android-reader's client side (separate repo).

Requirements: OPDS-01, OPDS-02, OPDS-03, OPDS-04.

**Authoritative source:** `docs/OPDS-AUTH-CONTRACT.md` — the wire contract both
repos agreed on. Every decision below is pinned by it; do not deviate without
updating that doc.
</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Token model & storage (contract §"server owns")
- New Prisma model `OpdsToken`: `id` (cuid), `userId` (FK → User, cascade delete, indexed), `tokenHash` (unique, the SHA-256 hex of the token — NOT the token), `label` (string, user-supplied), `createdAt`, `lastUsedAt` (nullable). The plaintext token is NEVER stored.
- Hashing: SHA-256 of the opaque token (these are ≥32-byte high-entropy secrets, so a fast cryptographic hash is correct — bcrypt is for low-entropy passwords). Look the token up by `tokenHash`; apply a constant-time compare (`node:crypto` `timingSafeEqual`) on the hash as defense-in-depth per the contract.
- Schema change requires a migration: `npx prisma migrate dev --name opds_tokens`. **HOST-RUN** (host/VM split — cannot run in the agent env). The plan must include this as a host step and commit the generated migration with the schema (per CLAUDE.md).

### Token format (contract §"wire contract")
- Opaque, URL-safe, 32 bytes of entropy: `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("base64url")` (no padding). Shown in plaintext exactly once at mint time; never logged.

### Auth guard (contract §"transport" + "failure")
- New helper `src/lib/opds-auth.ts`: `authenticateOpds(req): Promise<{ user } | null>`. Parses the `Authorization` header. Accepts BOTH `Basic base64(username ":" token)` AND `Bearer <token>`. Extracts the token (for Basic, split on the first `:`; the token is the password half), SHA-256 it, look up `OpdsToken` by hash, constant-time-confirm, return the owning user (resolved via the FK). On success, fire-and-forget bump `lastUsedAt` (do not block the response).
- The check lives IN each OPDS route handler, NOT in middleware — `src/auth.config.ts:40` deliberately exempts `/api/opds` from the cookie gate; KEEP that exemption (the comment "its own auth lands with the OPDS phase" is now this phase). Update the comment to reflect that OPDS auth is now enforced in-route.
- Apply the guard to ALL three current OPDS routes (`/api/opds`, `/api/opds/all`, `/api/opds/recent`) and document that any future OPDS path must call it too.
- Failure: `401` with header `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="homelab-reader OPDS"` and a short body. Success: `200` + the feed exactly as today.

### Progress attribution (OPDS-03)
- The OPDS-authenticated user (resolved by `authenticateOpds`) is the identity for any progress written in an OPDS context. If a dedicated OPDS-context progress write path is needed for android-reader, it authenticates with the same token guard and attributes to that user — never the cookie session. (The web reader's own `/api/progress` continues to use the cookie session unchanged.)

### Token management UI (contract §"web UI to mint/label/list/revoke")
- A settings page mirroring the existing `src/app/settings/users/` and `src/app/settings/libraries/` patterns: `src/app/settings/tokens/page.tsx` + a client manager component (mirror `UserManager.tsx`/`LibraryManager.tsx`).
- REST under the cookie session (web UI, per-user — a user manages ONLY their own tokens): `POST /api/opds-tokens` (mint → returns the plaintext token ONCE), `GET /api/opds-tokens` (list the caller's tokens: label, createdAt, lastUsedAt — NEVER the token/hash), `DELETE /api/opds-tokens/[id]` (revoke; 404 if not the caller's, matching the established by-id ownership pattern).
- Copy-once UX: the mint response shows the token with a copy affordance and a clear "you won't see this again" note.

### Claude's Discretion
- Exact component layout/styling of the tokens settings page (follow the calm, educational design tone and the existing settings pages).
- Whether `authenticateOpds` returns the full user or just the id (use whatever the routes need).
- Migration SQL specifics (generated by prisma migrate dev on the host).
</decisions>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- The whole point of this phase is interop: android-reader is being built against `docs/OPDS-AUTH-CONTRACT.md` in a separate repo. The server MUST match the wire contract exactly (Basic AND Bearer accepted; 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="homelab-reader OPDS"`; token = base64url ≥32 bytes; hashed at rest). OPDS-04's verification is conformance to that doc.
- Tokens are global-per-user for v1 (one token unlocks the whole catalog) — contract §"token scope".
</specifics>
